questions.q: How do you make DATEADD go backward instead of forward?
options: DATEADD can only move forward, never backward
Pass a negative number for the amount to add
Swap the order of the interval and date arguments
Use DATESUB instead of DATEADD
questions.explain: DATEADD(MONTH, -3, GETDATE()) computes three months ago — negative numbers subtract.

questions.q: What does DATEDIFF(DAY, OrderDate, DueDate) return?
options: The exact time of day DueDate occurs
The number of day boundaries crossed between OrderDate and DueDate
A boolean TRUE/FALSE indicating whether the dates match
The sum of OrderDate and DueDate
questions.explain: DATEDIFF measures the distance between two dates in the specified interval unit.

questions.q: What happens if you swap DATEDIFF's start and end date arguments?
options: The sign of the result flips (positive becomes negative, or vice versa)
The result is unaffected — order doesn't matter
The function throws an error
It automatically corrects the order for you
questions.explain: Order matters in DATEDIFF — reversing startDate and endDate negates the result.

questions.q: In 'WHERE OrderDate > DATEADD(YEAR, -1, GETDATE())', what is being computed?
options: The total count of orders from any date
Orders placed exactly one year from today
Orders placed within the last year, using DATEADD to compute the date one year before now
This filters out all orders entirely
questions.explain: DATEADD(YEAR, -1, GETDATE()) computes 'one year ago from right now,' and WHERE keeps only more recent orders.
